claims.text: Systematic controlled variation of annealing temperature is a suitable method for investigating the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Controlled annealing-temperature variation will enhance the mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The material before treatment is an as-cast FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The proposed intervention is annealing from 500°C to 1000°C for 1 hour.
Annealing is to be conducted under vacuum with a heating rate of 10°C/min and a cooling rate of 5°C/min.
Annealing temperature will alter the grain size of the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Annealing will induce or alter precipitate formation in the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Thermally activated diffusion is responsible for the annealing-induced microstructural changes.
Thermally activated precipitation processes contribute to the annealing response.
Annealing will increase yield strength by 15% relative to the as-cast state.
Annealing will increase ductility by 20% relative to the as-cast state.
Annealing temperatures below 500°C or above 1000°C lie outside the stated applicability boundary.
The actual mechanical properties may vary with processing conditions and the resulting microstructure.
Failure of both yield strength and ductility to increase by at least 10% after annealing at 800°C for 1 hour would falsify the hypothesis.
